name: Crispy Smashed Individual Meatloaves

ingredients.name: finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves
neutral oil, such as canola or vegetable

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack 15 cm from broiler element and preheat broiler on high setting. In a large bowl, combine bread and milk and let sit until bread is softened and milk is absorbed, about 5 minutes. Using a fork, mash bread mixture until it forms a paste. Add ground beef, ground pork, cheese, parsley, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, onion powder, and oregano. Using clean hands, gently mix until thoroughly combined.
Divide meat mixture into 8 equal portions. Gently shape each portion into a ball, pressing just firmly enough for it to hold together.
Heat a 30-cm heavy-bottomed stainless steel, carbon steel, or cast iron skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes. Increase heat to high. Add oil and swirl to coat skillet.

Season 2 meatballs evenly with 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper (about 1/8 teaspoon of kosher salt and pepper per patty). Add seasoned meatballs to skillet and cook, undisturbed, until just beginning to brown on bottom, 30 seconds to 1 minute. Flip meatballs so browned sides face up. Using a stiff metal spatula, firmly smash each ball into a patty measuring 10 to 11 cm in diameter and about 1.5 cm thick, using a second spatula to press down on the first if needed.

Cook patties, undisturbed, until a deep golden-brown crust develops on bottom, about 1 minute. Using edge of spatula, carefully scrape underneath patties to release them while keeping crust intact. Flip and cook until second sides are browned, about 1 minute. Transfer patties to a rimmed baking sheet. Repeat with remaining meatballs, seasoning 2 meatballs with 1/4 teaspoon each kosher salt and pepper before cooking each batch.

In a small bowl, whisk together ketchup, brown sugar, and apple cider vinegar. Spoon about 1 1/2 teaspoons glaze over each patty and spread into an even layer with the back of the spoon. Broil patties until glaze is bubbling and sticky, about 2 minutes. Serve immediately.

schema_metadata.keywords: meatloaf, smashed meatloaf, beef patties, smash burger, ground beef recipes, glazed meatloaf, smashed burgers

description: These quick-cooking smashed individual meatloaves have tender centers, deeply browned edges, and a sticky ketchup glaze, with no loaf pan or lengthy bake required.
notes:
Make-ahead and storage: The meat mixture can be prepared and shaped into balls up to 1 day ahead. Cover and refrigerate, then season as directed immediately before cooking.
These meatloaf patties are best eaten right away, while their edges are crisp, but leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days. To reheat, arrange patties on a rimmed baking sheet and bake in a 175°C (350°F) oven until heated through, about 8 minutes.
author: Leah Colins
